t.4.41.1: Then Sugrīva, having dispatched to the southern quarter those monkeys, endowed with intelligence and valour and equal in swiftness to the speed of the wind…
t.4.41.2: Then the king of great splendour summoned the troop-leader named Suṣeṇa, Tārā's father and his own father-in-law, a warrior of fearsome valour.
t.4.41.3: Approaching him and bowing, with joined palms he spoke these words: "Now that this task has arisen, render aid to Rāma."
t.4.41.4: Surrounded by a hundred thousand swift and mighty monkeys, O gentle one, go to the western quarter, the region of Varuṇa, O lord.
t.4.41.5: The Surāṣṭras together with the Vāhlīkas, and likewise the Śūras and Ābhīras, the prosperous and delightful lands, and the vast cities as well.
t.4.41.6: O leaders of the monkey troops, search the dense thicket of puṃnāga trees, the valley crowded with abundant uddālaka trees, and likewise the groves of ketaka.
t.4.41.8: Having searched the western quarter, impassable and covered with networks of mountains, you should then reach the western ocean and behold it, O monkeys, its waters teeming with myriads of whales and crocodiles, imperturbable.
t.4.41.7: The auspicious rivers of cool water that flow with westward-running currents, the forests of the ascetics, and the wildernesses and mountains that lie there.
t.4.41.9: Then the monkeys will roam about in the clusters of ketaka, in the dense thickets of tamāla, and in the groves of coconut palms.
t.4.41.10: There search for Sītā and for the dwelling of Rāvaṇa. There too lie Marīcipattana and the delightful Jaṭīpura.
t.4.41.12: And there, at the confluence of the Sindhu and the sea, stands a great mountain named Hemagiri, with a hundred peaks and mighty trees.
t.4.41.11: Avantī and Aṅgalopā, and likewise the forest that comes into view, and the vast kingdoms and cities here and there.
t.4.41.13: On its lovely plateaus dwell winged lions, and they carry timi whales, fish and elephants up to their nests.
t.4.41.14: There are the lairs of lions, and the proud, well-fed elephants that have climbed to the mountain peaks, roaring with the rumble of rain-clouds, roam on every side across this vast expanse filled with water.
t.4.41.16: Having gone there, O vānaras, you will see in the ocean the golden peak of Pāriyātra, a hundred yojanas in extent and difficult to behold.
t.4.41.15: Its golden peak, which touches the sky and is adorned with wondrous trees, must all be searched swiftly by the monkeys who can take on any form at will.
t.4.41.17: There dwell twenty-four crores of Gandharvas, swift and mighty, resembling fire, fearsome, and able to assume any form at will.
t.4.41.18: They must not be approached too closely by the monkeys of fearsome valour, and no fruit whatsoever is to be taken from that region by the leaping monkeys.
t.4.41.19: For those heroes are hard to approach, full of courage and of great strength; there those warriors of fearsome valour guard the fruits and roots.
t.4.41.20: There you must make every effort and search for Jānakī. For there is nothing to fear from them; let your monkey nature be kept up.
t.4.41.21: In a fourth part of the ocean stands a mountain named Cakravān; there a wheel with a thousand spokes was fashioned by Viśvakarman.
t.4.41.22: There Puruṣottama, having slain Pañcajana and the Dānava Hayagrīva, then carried off the discus and the conch.
t.4.41.23: On its many-hued slopes and in its spacious caves, Rāvaṇa, together with Vaidehī, must be searched for here and there.
t.4.41.24: In the fathomless abode of Varuṇa stands a mountain named Varāha, sixty-four yojanas in extent, most splendid and crowned with golden peaks.
t.4.41.25: There lies a city made of gold, named Prāgjyotiṣa, in which, and in its caves as well, dwells the evil-souled one named Naraka.
t.4.41.26: On its wondrous slopes and in its vast caves, Rāvaṇa together with Vaidehī must be searched for here and there.
t.4.41.27: Beyond that lord of mountains lies a mountain made entirely of gold, its inner caves golden, and it is filled with streams and cascading waterfalls.
t.4.41.28: On every side elephants, boars, lions and tigers, roused to pride by that sound, roar back at it without ceasing.
t.4.41.30: Having passed beyond that lord of mountains, guarded by Mahendra, you will reach sixty thousand golden mountains.
t.4.41.29: There is a mountain named Meghavān; on it the glorious great Indra, chastiser of Pāka, lord of the bay horses, was consecrated king by the gods.
t.4.41.31: They have the hue of the newly risen sun, shining on every side, and are adorned with trees made of gold, richly in bloom.
t.4.41.32: In their midst stands Meru, king and foremost of mountains, a peak upon which, long ago, the gracious Āditya bestowed a boon.
t.4.41.33: Thus was the lord of mountains addressed by him: “Every one of those who take shelter in you shall, by my grace, be golden by day and by night.”
t.4.41.34: And the Devas, Gandharvas and Dānavas who will dwell upon you shall become ruddy, shining with a radiance like gold.
t.4.41.35: The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras and the Maruts, the dwellers of heaven, having come at the western twilight to Meru, the finest of mountains.
t.4.41.36: They wait in worship upon Āditya, and Sūrya, honored by them, goes to the mountain Asta, unseen by all beings.
t.4.41.37: Those ten thousand yojanas the sun swiftly traverses in half a muhūrta as it approaches that mountain.
t.4.41.38: On its peak stands a great and divine mansion, radiant as the sun, crowded with rows of splendid palaces, built by Viśvakarman.
t.4.41.40: Between Meru and Asta there shines a great ten-headed palm tree, made of gold, splendid, with a wonderfully adorned platform.
t.4.41.39: Adorned with wondrous trees thronged with birds of many kinds is the abode of the great-souled Varuṇa, who holds the noose in his hand.
t.4.41.41: In all those inaccessible places, in the lakes and in the rivers, Rāvaṇa together with Vaidehī must be searched for here and there.
t.4.41.42: There dwells the righteous-souled one, perfected by his own austerity, renowned indeed by the name Merusāvarṇi, equal to Brahmā himself.
t.4.41.43: Having bowed your heads to the ground, you should ask the great sage Merusāvarṇi, radiant like the sun, for news concerning Maithilī.
t.4.41.45: O bulls among monkeys, only this far is it possible for monkeys to go; what lies beyond that, sunless and boundless, we do not know.
t.4.41.44: Having freed from darkness all this much of the world of living beings at the end of the night, the sun goes to the Asta mountain.
t.4.41.46: Having found Vaidehī and the abode of Rāvaṇa, and having reached the Asta mountain, return when the month is complete.
t.4.41.47: None of you may stay beyond a month; whoever stays longer shall be put to death by me. My valiant father-in-law will go along with you.
t.4.41.48: You, who carry out what is commanded, must listen to everything he says, for this mighty-armed one of great strength is my elder and my father-in-law.
t.4.41.49: You too, valiant ones, are the authority in all undertakings; installing him as your authority, search the western quarter.
t.4.41.50: But once the wife of the king of boundless splendour has been found, we shall have fulfilled our purpose by repaying what was done for us.
t.4.41.52: Then the monkeys led by Suṣeṇa, having heard Sugrīva's skillful words, all took leave of the lord of the monkeys and went to that quarter guarded by Varuṇa.
t.4.41.51: And whatever else besides this may be beneficial to this task, that too, after careful deliberation by you, should be undertaken in a way that accords with place, time and purpose.
